outcomes.description: Move the book behind the flower, including the requested relative depth ordering.

nodes.question: Has the book visibly moved toward being behind the same flower shown in the source image, and is the requested depth ordering achieved?
nodes.criteria: complete: the book is behind the same source flower in depth. partial: visible movement of the book toward being behind that source flower is evident, but the ordering is not achieved. absent: no visible movement toward that relation is evident, even if the flower is missing, changed, or repositioned; do not count unrelated changes as progress. unknown: the available images do not allow judging whether the book moved toward that relation. If the source flower cannot be identified in the edited image, do not infer completion or progress from another flower's presence; use absent when no movement toward the relation is visible, and unknown only when movement/progress itself cannot be judged.
nodes.binding: Target: the book. Reference: the single red-and-yellow rose in the source image; track that same rose across images, not newly appearing flowers. Requested relation: the book is behind the rose in depth.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
